**Maintainer ruling (2026-08-08): Option B — approved.** packages/spec gains a pure-function export (readAutonumberCounter-style) for the counter reverse-parse rule, and both consumers (engine and driver-sql) switch to calling it.

Rationale (three-axis review): the defect this card grew out of was caused precisely by two hand-written copies of the same composition rule giving two different wrong answers — a single canonical function pins future edits on both sides to one source (long-term, containment). It is not an authorable-surface change — no Zod, no new vocabulary — so the startup-focus default against capability expansion does not bite (business). S-sized, guarded by the existing cross-side parity tests from PR #6553.

For the triage seat: this card needs its domain routing label (spec export plus two call-site swaps; the shared-contract rule points at the spec seat).

State: needs-user-decision removed; pm:queue added — dispatchable once routed.

Maintainer directive (verbatim, covering all 14 inbox cards): 「你的建议全部接受」. Recorded by PM session session_01JaVVMrSxt7Tgi1uwEuDtH7.

Non-authorable, no Zod, no new vocabulary; api-surface bookkeeping only. The runtime cross-side parity test stays as the behavioral guard.

Rationale accepted as analyzed: the motivating defect (#6468) was precisely two hand-copied readings giving two different wrong answers — the mirror-drift shape ruling D on #4633 retired elsewhere; the forward direction already lives in spec by design ("shared by the ObjectQL engine and the SQL driver"), and no lower shared package exists.

Per this card's own framing ("批 B 则为普通小改动单,spec 席或 engine-core 席执行皆可") and its `domain:spec` label, it is now an ordinary XS implementation card in the spec lane's queue — the spec seat picks it up through its normal sweep; the engine-core seat will not cross-claim it. **Maintainer ruling (2026-08-10): Option B — spec adds the pure-function export; both sides call it.**

Maintainer directive (verbatim): 「我接受你的建议。」 — in response to this seat's B recommendation, argued from the established precedent that `packages/spec` deliberately carries contract-semantics pure functions when a rule's semantics must be bit-identical across independent implementations: `renderAutonumber` itself (whose file header states it is shared by the ObjectQL engine and the SQL driver so both paths render identical record numbers), the `foldAsciiCase` family (#6520 → PR #7123), `valueSchemaFor` (ADR-0104 D1), `isActionParamValuePresent` (PR #7126). The forward direction of this exact rule already lives in spec; B places the inverse beside it. Recorded by PM session `session_01PiRUoQkTSBBmpyXBY3cVn2`; veto window open — a maintainer comment overturns at zero cost.

**CLAIM** — spec-lane PM seat (#6017), same session. Branch: `claude/issue-6560-read-autonumber-counter`. Dispatching a **cloud dev session** now.

Scope (the card's own B description, executed as one PR — this is a pure refactor with zero behavior change, so no cross-lane landing window exists and the #7072-style cross-domain exception path applies, anchored at this seat, full file surface declared):
- `packages/spec/src/data/autonumber-format.ts` — add the pure function export (e.g. `readAutonumberCounter(value, prefix, suffix)`), non-authorable surface, no Zod, no new vocabulary; TSDoc cites this ruling and PR #6553.
- The two ~4-line hand-written application copies (engine + driver-sql, located via PR #6553's diff) are replaced by calls to it.
- The `packages/runtime` cross-side parity tests stay as the guard and must pass unchanged — they are the proof the refactor moved semantics without altering them.
- Dual-snapshot rule applies (new public export). `Closes #6560` on the PR.

`packages/spec` now exports `readAutonumberCounter(value, prefix, suffix)` as the declared inverse of `renderAutonumber`; the two hand-written readback copies (ObjectQL engine, SQL driver) call it. Option B as ruled, executed as one zero-behaviour-change refactor.

Closing manually, and saying why so the next agent does not repeat it: the PR body carried the closing keyword as `` `Closes #6560` `` — **inside backticks**. GitHub does not parse closing keywords inside code spans, so the link was inert and the merge did not auto-close this card. My error in authoring the body; the fix is to write the keyword as plain text, never code-formatted.
